title: Persistent Photo-Enhancement of Molecular Orbital Excitations in the Kondo Insulator FeSb$_2$
authors: Ke-Jun Xu, Nathan Giles-Donovan, Paulina Majchrzak, Abhi Suthar, Matthias Hepting, Marco Trento, Giacomo Ghiringhelli, Elizabeth Skoropata, Hiroki Ueda, Eugenio Paris, Biaolong Liu, Elia Razzoli, Wei-Sheng Lee, Thomas P. Devereaux, Zhi-Xun Shen, Dung-Hai Lee, Robert J. Birgeneau
abstract: When insulators are excited by photons with above-gap energies, photo-doped carriers are transiently generated. Typically, orbital excitations weaken and broaden due to increased screening by these transient carriers, followed by a few-ps recovery via phonon thermalization. Here we report the observation of anomalous dynamics of many-body molecular orbital excitations in the narrow-gap Kondo insulator FeSb$_2$. In the pumped X-ray absorption spectra following excitation with 1~$μ$m photons, we observe a transient transfer of absorption intensity from the delocalized states at the main absorption peak to the localized molecular orbital states at the pre-edge. At the resonance of the low-energy molecular orbital excitations, the pumped resonant inelastic X-ray spectra show an approximately 30\% intensity increase at a pump fluence of 11 mJ/cm$^2$ concomitant with the emergence of an energy gain feature. While the energy gain feature disappears after about 1-2~ps, the increased molecular orbital excitation intensities partially persist for at least 50~ps with no discernible energy shift. These observations require the invocation of a many-body excitation picture beyond single particle population changes.
summary: This work reports on the anomalous dynamics of molecular orbital excitations in the Kondo insulator FeSb2 using time-resolved X-ray spectroscopy. Researchers observed a transient, persistent enhancement of these excitations following optical pumping. These findings strongly argue for the necessity of a many-body excitation picture to accurately describe the photo-induced electronic state of the material.
main_problem: The study investigates the anomalous dynamics of many-body molecular orbital excitations in the Kondo insulator FeSb2 following optical excitation.
main_result: The research observed a transient, persistent enhancement of molecular orbital excitation intensities for at least 50 ps, which requires a many-body excitation picture beyond simple single-particle changes.
method: The experiment utilized time-resolved X-ray Absorption Spectroscopy (trXAS) and time-resolved Resonant Inelastic X-ray Scattering (trRIXS) at the SwissFEL facility.
model_or_system: The physical system is the Kondo insulator FeSb2, characterized by a gap formed by hybridization between localized magnetic moments and delocalized conduction electrons. The analysis focuses on the interplay between these localized and delocalized electronic states.
key_observables: Transient intensity transfer from delocalized states (main peak) to localized molecular orbital states (pre-edge); $\sim 30\%$ intensity increase at M1/M2 molecular orbital energies in trRIXS.
important_parameters: Pump fluence of $11 	ext{ mJ/cm}^2$; persistence time scale of at least $50 	ext{ ps}$; excitation energy from $1 \mu	ext{m}$ photons.
main_assumptions: The persistence of the signal suggests a metastable state requiring a many-body excitation picture, moving beyond single-particle population changes.
figures_summary: Figures show the time-delay dependence of XAS intensity (Fig. 1) and RIXS spectra (Fig. 2, 3), illustrating the initial enhancement of molecular orbital intensities followed by partial persistence over tens of picoseconds.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first presenting the initial observation of intensity transfer via trXAS, followed by detailed analysis using trRIXS to quantify the enhancement and its subsequent decay/persistence over time delays.
why_interesting: The observation of persistent, enhanced molecular orbital excitations in a correlated insulator provides direct experimental evidence for non-equilibrium many-body dynamics, which is crucial for understanding charge transfer and excitation lifetimes in strongly correlated materials.
